A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCGNet research. All 23 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B, are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on 12 datasets, component ablations, missing-input robustness tests and parameter analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original forecasting results, ablations, robustness experiments and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The Variational Generator, Graph Structure Aligner, Graph Refiner and training losses are unchanged. Section 3.4 adds attribution for the existing top-k sparsification procedure without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 datasets and scenarios involving available, unavailable or partially missing exogenous variables. Correcting 'Raperl' to 'Rapel' does not change dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks, robustness tests and appendix comparisons. TimeFilter is newly named as a methodological source in Section 3.4, not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The data splits, MSE/MAE metrics, lookback windows, forecasting horizons, masking procedures and controlled-hyperparameter evaluations remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: The component ablations, missing-value robustness tests, forecast visualizations, parameter sensitivity studies and lookback-length analyses are identical in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates and averages across horizons or masking ratios. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Result entries, numerical values and plotted findings are unchanged in Tables 1–5 and 7–10 and Figures 4–7. For example, Table 1 retains GCGNet's NP horizon-24 MSE/MAE of 0.197/0.233.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, including graph construction, training objectives and the appendix MLP fusion formulation, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about robust joint temporal/channel modeling and forecasting performance on 12 datasets.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning degeneration prevention, noise robustness, exogenous-variable availability and ablation or sensitivity outcomes are unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same dataset descriptions, implementation environment, drop-last setting, baseline fusion details and code/data access statements. The added attribution supplies no new implementation settings.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 now explicitly states that top-k sparsification follows TimeFilter (Hu et al., 2025b). That work was already cited in the introduction and bibliography; the reference set and broader positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized spelling corrections, including 'Raperl' to 'Rapel', and revises the sparsification sentence to include attribution. Section organization and appendix prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 corrects 'Graph Leaner' to 'Graph Learner'; Table 3 corrects a caption typo; Table 4 corrects 'Mask Tpye' and slightly adjusts header formatting. The displays otherwise retain their content and organization.

improvement.justification: Explicitly crediting TimeFilter for the existing sparsification step improves attribution transparency, while the typo and table-header corrections modestly improve presentation. The method, empirical evidence and appendices remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
